title: United Airlines Bans Unauthorized AI Agents, Starting Battle For Control In AI Commerce
summary: As announced on the United Airlines site, the airline now restricts all unauthorized AI agents on its site from making material changes to reservations and purchased tickets, meaing that if a third-party AI agent, bot, browser extension, or browser feature searches, books, buys, manages, or collects information on United.com or the United app for you, […]
body_markdown:
As announced on the United Airlines site,[the airline now restricts all unauthorized AI agents on its site](https://www.united.com/en/us/fly/help-center/digital-trust-center/artificial-intelligence/third-party-ai-agents.html) from making material changes to reservations and purchased tickets, meaing that if a third-party AI agent, bot, browser extension, or browser feature searches, books, buys, manages, or collects information on United.com or the United app for you, and United hasn’t given permission, it’s unauthorized. United explains further in its communication, “This data helps us meet regulatory requirements while also enabling us to deliver personalized experiences and improvements to our products and services. This is a responsibility we take seriously.”


United does not yet work with any AI agent providers for authorized AI agent access. It is worth noting that[Amazon](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/01/jpmorgan-amazon-ai-agents-meta-muse.html) ,[Booking.com](https://tourismintel.ai/newsletter/booking-com-cuts-the-phone-line-as-ai-agents-take-the-trip) ,[eBay](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1030838/ebay-ai-agents-meta-muse-agentic-shopping) ,[JPMorgan Chase](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/01/jpmorgan-amazon-ai-agents-meta-muse.html) , and[Target](https://www.theverge.com/report/1015811/ai-shopping-agents-blocked-amazon-the-realreal-target-meta-muse) also have varying levels of restrictions on AI agents accessing their site or customer-facing channels.


Organizations like United are restricting unauthorized AI agents for the following reasons:


1. Taking proactive measures to own the customer experience, although blocking all AI agent access long-term may be counterproductive
2. An org’s existing identity and access management and fraud management solutions and layers may not be sufficient to detect and manage AI agents
3. To minimize an org becoming just an AI “middleman” to broker transactions: Restricting third-party AI agents also preserves organizational control over AI agents and avoids AI agents overloading a site with excessive queries that creates service degradation
4. To minimize existing negative experiences: Unvetted and potentially fraudulent AI agents expose companies to additional liabilities and challenges, and AI agents have been hacking e-commerce sites at[$25 per site](https://gambit.security/blog-posts/autonomous-ai-agents-online-retailers-25-a-company)
5. Lacking the appropriate defense tooling: While AI agent runtime controls and know-your-agent validation are emerging technologies, they may still struggle at scale in prime-time, mission-critical use
6. Reducing exposure to fines and sanctions: Any loss of personally identifiable information caused by an AI agent might also negatively impact an organization’s regulatory compliance and brand reputation
7. Waiting out for mature technology and standards: Until liability schemes, mature AI agent verification, and authentication tools with proper “human in the loop” decisions emerge, many B2C organizations will likely limit third-party agent use on their commerce sites


We recommend that B2C commerce sites: 1) define the set of, and allow only, well-known and verified AI agent providers (Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI) to act on behalf of their customers; 2) mandate short-term token-based AI agent access rights management and delegation, including explicit human-performed step-up authentication; 3) err on the side of caution when customer AI agents try to make high-risk, high-value transactions (such as ticket purchases and reservation changes, in United’s case); and 4) audit all agent actions in detail.
